subject: 6-Week Checkpoint: OKR alignment, scope trim & dependency commitments
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@orbitcloud.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: 6-Week Checkpoint: OKR alignment, scope trim & dependency commitments

Team —

Quick 6-week pulse ahead of the QBR planning week. I reviewed the OKR dashboards and talked to a few PMs; there are three items we need to resolve this week so the QBR pack doesn't change last minute: 

1) Latency optimization (OBJ-1): original goal: "Reduce tail P95 inference latency by 20% for hosted API." Current reality: telemetry shows ~8–12% improvement on test workloads after the new kernels. Achievable delta to announce with confidence looks closer to 10–12% unless we commit extra infra or scope the rollout to fewer models.

2) Dedicated capacity rollout (OBJ-2): sales is pushing OrbitCloud as a pilot for Nov. They need a committed SLA window and autoscale test sign-off.

3) Cost optimization initiative (OBJ-3): the Optimize recommendations require 2 s/w weeks of engineering to validate quantization profiles per model family.

Proposals (short):
- Re-scope OBJ-1 public target to 10% improvement for Q4, keep 20% as stretch for H1 next year.
- For OrbitCloud pilot, we can target a limited regional SLA and a canary on one model family; will require reserved node capacity for 2 weeks and a runbook.
- Prioritize 1 engineer sprint (2 engineers for 2 weeks) to validate top-3 quantization profiles; defer broader audit to Jan.

Action asks: please reply with a clear commit or blocker by EOD Tuesday (10/13). Specifically: 
- Markus: can infra allocate the short-term reserved capacity for the pilot and is a 10% latency public target acceptable?
- Karthik: what headcount/time can you commit to the quantization validation sprint?
- Laura: do we need to escalate for credits/partner discounts for OrbitCloud or can sales absorb?

Attachments: Q4 OKR slice (spreadsheet) and a lightweight action grid.

Thanks — I want to lock these before we hand the QBR pack to growth.

— Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: q4_okr_slice_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: 6w_checkpoint_action_grid.md (text)]

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@orbitcloud.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 6-Week Checkpoint: OKR alignment, scope trim & dependency commitments

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Agree with a conservative public target and keeping 20% as a stretch. A couple of clarifications from infra: 

> Re-scope OBJ-1 public target to 10% improvement for Q4, keep 20% as stretch for H1 next year.

- We can mark 10% as the official Q4 communication. To get to 20% we'd need additional kernel work + an extra perf engineer for 2 months (or equivalent contractor).

> For OrbitCloud pilot, we can target a limited regional SLA and a canary on one model family; will require reserved node capacity for 2 weeks and a runbook.

- We can provide reserved capacity for 2 weeks for the pilot, but need sign-off on the exact models and expected qps so we can pre-warm caches. Also will need a support rotation during the pilot window.

I don't think we need exec-level escalation yet; Laura, if bookings/credits come into play we should surface to finance.

Action from me: I'll draft a short infra commitment note with required capacity specs and a runbook checklist by EOD Monday.

— Markus
Director, Systems Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, sales@orbitcloud.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 6-Week Checkpoint: OKR alignment, scope trim & dependency commitments

Vanessa / Markus —

We can staff the quantization validation sprint but need to be explicit about acceptance criteria and model list. Proposed commitment: 
- 2 engineers (infra + model infra) for 2 weeks starting 10/19. Focus: top-3 customer-facing model families (chat-gen-v2, embed-large, rerank-lite).
- Deliverable: validated quantization profiles per model family, a perf delta matrix, and a rollback plan.

Open asks from infra: 
- Confirmation of model list by EOD 10/15 so we can reserve infra.
- Budget approval for temporary instance types (we'll need 1x p4-equivalent reserved for the 2-week window).

If we get model confirmation and budget sign-off, we can hit the sprint dates. Otherwise we shift to Nov and it will miss the QBR timeline.

I'll attach a short runbook and cost estimate in a follow-up.

— Karthik
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quant_sprint_runbook.md (text)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@orbitcloud.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 6-Week Checkpoint: OKR alignment, scope trim & dependency commitments

Thanks — concise and actionable. I approve the conservative public target (10% for Q4) and will greenlight the two-week reserved capacity for the OrbitCloud pilot provided we limit it to the single model family and a firm start/end date.

Decisions: 
- OBJ-1: Public target = 10% for Q4, maintain internal stretch to 20% (H1).
- OrbitCloud pilot: approved reserved capacity for 10/25–11/08; sales to confirm model names and expected qps by 10/15. Pricing/credits: finance will review; no exec credits needed if pilot is limited.
- Quantization sprint: approve 2 engineers for 2 weeks starting 10/19 conditional on model list confirmation and a $7k temporary infra budget.

Next steps (owners & deadlines):
- Sales (OrbitCloud) -> confirm model list & qps (by 10/15).
- Markus -> infra commitment note + runbook checklist (by 10/12).
- Karthik -> cost estimate + sprint plan (by 10/14).
- Vanessa -> update QBR pack and public OKR language (by 10/16).

I'll set a 30-min sync Thursday to close any loose ends. Adding the JIRA ticket INF-3172 to track the pilot tasks and the Google doc link to the pack.

— Laura Bennett
Chief Operating Officer, Redwood Inference
